subject: Archaeology
title: Carnac: Thousands of Standing Stones
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Carnac: Thousands of Standing Stones.

hook.text: In Brittany, France, over 3,000 standing stones march in perfect rows across the countryside for two miles.

buildup.text: The Carnac stones were erected between 4500 and 3300 BCE — before Stonehenge, the pyramids, or writing.

discovery.text: The alignments run east to west in parallel rows. Some stones are 12 feet tall; others barely reach knee height.

twist.text: Nobody knows their purpose. Theories include astronomical markers, ritual pathways, and earthquake detectors.

climax.text: Local legend says the stones are Roman soldiers turned to stone by Merlin. Archaeology offers no better explanation yet.

punchline.text: Three thousand stones in perfect rows. Zero explanation after 6,000 years.

quiz.question: What makes the Carnac stone alignments mysterious?
options: They contain inscriptions in an undeciphered language
Nobody knows their purpose despite 6,000 years of existence
They were moved from a quarry over 500 miles away

details.summary: Carnac in Brittany, France, contains over 3,000 standing stones arranged in long parallel rows stretching for kilometers. Erected between 4500 and 3300 BCE, these megalithic alignments are the largest concentration of standing stones in the world, with purposes still debated.
details.whyItMatters: Carnac's sheer scale reveals that Neolithic communities could organize massive construction projects without centralized states. The stones challenge us to understand the beliefs that motivated such extraordinary collective effort.
takeaways: Over 3,000 standing stones stretch for kilometers at Carnac
They were erected between 4500 and 3300 BCE
Carnac has the world's largest concentration of standing stones

faq.question: What were the Carnac stones for?
faq.answer: Theories include astronomical alignments, ceremonial pathways, territorial markers, and ancestor worship sites. No single explanation accounts for all features. The rows may have served multiple functions over their long period of construction and use.

faq.question: How were the Carnac stones erected?
faq.answer: Using levers, ropes, ramps, and coordinated human labor. The largest stones weigh over 300 tons. Experimental archaeology has shown that teams of several hundred people could raise these stones using wooden frameworks and counterweights available in the Neolithic.
